step1_analysis.description: A 3-stage CMOS operational amplifier featuring parallel PMOS and NMOS folded-cascode input stages, intermediate common-source inverters, and a nested Class-AB cascoded output stage. It is designed for robust signal interfacing in a biochemical microsensor.

paper_reference.title: A CMOS Multiparameter Biochemical Microsensor With Temperature Control and Signal Interfacing

sky130_expected.calculation: 3 stages (folded cascode + inverter + cascoded output). Each stage provides ~40 dB of gain (gm * ro). Total gain = 40 + 40 + 40 = 120 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cascoded output and 3-stage architecture yield extremely high DC gain, limited primarily by the output impedance of the short-channel devices in SKY130.

sky130_expected.calculation: UGBW ≈ gm1 / (2 * pi * Cload). With gm1 ≈ 133 uS (10uA bias, Vov=0.15V) and Cload = 15 pF, UGBW ≈ 1.4 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Since there are no internal compensation capacitors in the netlist, the amplifier relies on load capacitance for dominant-pole compensation.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin at unity gain frequency

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the separation between the dominant pole (at the output node with 15pF load) and non-dominant poles (at internal nodes N13, N18, N0, N1).
sky130_expected.reasoning: A 15pF load capacitor is added to ensure stability for this 3-stage uncompensated OTA topology.

sky130_expected.calculation: Total current ≈ 120 uA (20uA per tail, 20uA per folded branch, 20uA per inverter, 20uA output quiescent). Power = 1.8V * 120uA = 216 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for SKY130 1.8V supply. The 0.25W reported in the paper is for the entire multiparameter microsensor chip, not just this single op-amp.

slew_rate.description: Maximum rate of change of the output voltage

sky130_expected.calculation: Class-AB output stage allows dynamic current boosting. Max current is limited by Vsg of output devices when driven to rails. I_max ≈ 470 uA. SR = I_max / Cload = 470uA / 15pF ≈ 31 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The Class-AB nature of the output stage (driven by the intermediate inverters) provides a slew rate significantly higher than a standard Class-A OTA.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC gain, UGBW, phase margin, power consumption, and slew rate of the RRIO Op-Amp. Uses a large L/C feedback network for closed-loop DC biasing and open-loop AC measurement, then alters them for transient step response.
